title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
description:
# Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
## CISA Approach
- **Provide Technical Guidance and Risk Management Strategies for PQC Implementation (** [**Executive Order [EO] 14412**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/securing-the-nation-against-advanced-cryptographic-attacks/) **)**: CISA consults with NIST and the National Security Agency (NSA) to provide federal departments and agencies with technical guidance on PQC implementation, including best practices and risk management strategies. Additionally, CISA works with Sector Risk Management Agencies (SRMA) to assist critical infrastructure owners and operators in developing PQC migration planning.
- **Execution of PQC Migration****(** [**OMB Memorandum M-26-15**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/M-26-15-Execution-of-the-Migration-to-Post-Quantum-Cryptography.pdf)**&**[**OMB Memorandum M-23-02**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/M-23-02-M-Memo-on-Migrating-to-Post-Quantum-Cryptography.pdf)**)**: CISA helps drive the federal migration to PQC through migration planning, working with cloud service providers, identifying systems most vulnerable to quantum attacks, and assessing cryptographic inventory submissions from across the Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB).
- [**Quantum Technology Protection**](https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/protecting-quantum-science-and-technology) **(** [**EO 14413**](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/ushering-in-the-next-frontier-of-quantum-innovation/) **)**:CISA supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) as a member of the [Quantum Information Science and Technology Counterintelligence Protection Team (QCPT)](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/ushering-in-the-next-frontier-of-quantum-innovation/). By delivering cybersecurity and physical security services across the nation, CISA helps DHS secure the quantum supply chain against emerging threats.
- [**Product Category Identification**](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/product-categories-technologies-use-post-quantum-cryptography-standards)**(** [**EO 14306**](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/06/11/2025-10804/sustaining-select-efforts-to-strengthen-the-nations-cybersecurity-and-amending-executive-order-13694)**)**: CISA develops and regularly updates a list of product categories that include technologies that support or plan to support PQC standard algorithms.

## PQC Related Resources
### NIST Guidance
- [**Frequently Asked Questions About PQC and Migration Guidance**](https://pages.nist.gov/nccoe-migration-post-quantum-cryptography/FAQ/index.html). This page explains how to navigate the shift to quantum-resistant encryption—covering key topics like building a cryptographic inventory, adopting new standards, and preparing organizations for future quantum threats.
- [**PQC Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)**](https://csrc.nist.gov/news/2024/postquantum-cryptography-fips-approved) **.** On August 13, 2024, NIST approved three PQC standards—FIPS 203, FIPS 204, and FIPS 205—to help protect federal systems from future quantum computing threats.
- [**Post-Quantum Cryptography Project**](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/post-quantum-cryptography) **.** The NIST PQC Project leads the effort to evaluate and standardize cryptographic algorithms that can withstand quantum computing threats.
- [**Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program**](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-algorithm-validation-program) **.** This program uses automated testing to check whether vendors’ FIPS-approved cryptographic algorithms work correctly before they can be certified by National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program-accredited labs and listed as validated.

### GSA Guidance
- [**PQC Buyers Guide**](https://buy.gsa.gov/api/system/files/documents/final-508c-pqc_buyer-s_guide_2025.pdf) **.** GSA designed this guide to enable agencies to safeguard existing systems from both classical and quantum computer-based risks and maintain the confidentiality and integrity of data communications.

### DHS Guidance
- [**DHS PQC Roadmap**](https://www.dhs.gov/quantum) **.** This roadmap, jointly produced by DHS and NIST, outlines the risks posed by advances in quantum computing and guides organizations in preparing for the transition to PQC through inventory, planning, and risk-based modernization of cryptographic systems.

### NSA Guidance
- [**CNSA 2.0 and Quantum Computing FAQ**](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Sep/07/2003071836/-1/-1/1/CSI_CNSA_2.0_FAQ_.PDF). This document clarifies Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0) requirements for National Security Systems (NSS) and recommended guidance for the Department of War (DoW) and the Defense Industrial Base (DIB).
- [**NSA Post-Quantum Cybersecurity Resources**](https://www.nsa.gov/Cybersecurity/Post-Quantum-Cybersecurity-Resources/). This resources page outlines NSA’s guidance on quantum-resistant cryptography, naming approved algorithms under Committee on National Security Systems Policy 15 and advising caution with quantum key distribution until current technical limits are resolved.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
description:
# Post-Quantum Cryptography
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), in partnership with the Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), has released a roadmap to help organizations protect their data and systems and to reduce risks related to the advancement of quantum computing technology.

DHS’s new guidance will help organizations prepare for the transition to post-quantum cryptography by identifying, prioritizing, and protecting potentially vulnerable data, algorithms, protocols, and systems.

In March, DHS [outlined the vision for cybersecurity resilience](https://www.dhs.gov/news/2021/03/31/secretary-mayorkas-outlines-his-vision-cybersecurity-resilience) and identified the transition to post-quantum encryption as a priority. DHS also issued internal policy guidance to drive the Department’s own preparedness efforts and is conducting a macro-level analysis to inform the government’s action and ensure a smooth and equitable transition.

## DHS Approach
### Planning for the DHS Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
This work focuses on the development and implementation of Departmental guidance on the transition to post-quantum cryptography within DHS and its Components. This guidance directs the Department to prepare for transition to new post-quantum cryptography standards when available from NIST following the quantum roadmap.

## Roadmap
In partnership with NIST, DHS created a guide to provide relevant stakeholders with concrete and achievable steps they can take now to prepare their organizations for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.

1. Organizations should direct their Chief Information Officers to increase their engagement with standards developing organizations for latest developments relating to necessary algorithm and dependent protocol changes.
14. Using the inventory and prioritization information, organizations should develop a plan for systems transitions upon publication of the new post-quantum cryptographic standard. Cybersecurity officials should provide guidance for creating transition plans.

## Quantum Background
DHS will prioritize preparing for the challenge of post-quantum cryptography without purchasing or implementing any tools or solutions until the new standards are approved by NIST.

Building on the 2024 statement, the G7 CEG developed this high-level roadmap to inform senior leaders on the types of activities that may help organizations transition to post-quantum cryptography in a coordinated, timely, and objective-driven way in advance of future risks.

## TLP: CLEAR
This roadmap may help these entities better understand the importance of quantum-resistant cryptography to the financial sector and the potential time constraints for migration.

## Considerations for Potential Timelines for Transition to Quantum-Resistant
7The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is establishing strategic timelines for transitioning to quantum-resistant cryptography to inform the efforts and timelines of government agencies, industry, and standards organizations.

## TLP: CLEAR
- Monitor progress with post-quantum cryptography migration and share information across jurisdictions, support transitional efforts, and encourage jurisdictional consistency. As the technology and our understanding of it develops, timelines may be revisited as needed.
- Monitor evolving threats, technology, and migration lessons learned and consider updating resources to support organizations.

title: Quantum-safe migration: An opportunity to modernize ...
description:
#### Cybersecurity
Timeline for the migration to quantum safety, with key compliance and technological milestones Image: HSBC/evolutionQ

Here, we set out a new vision for quantum safety: that the quantum-safe migration is a unique opportunity for organizations to rethink and modernize their cybersecurity strategies, elevating cryptography as an asset that enhances business resilience.

## Building a quantum-safe future
### 1. Cryptographic inventory
Building resilience starts with understanding an organization’s cryptographic landscape.

### 3. Cryptographic defence-in-depth
Cryptographic defence-in-depth leverages multiple layers of cryptography to mitigate the risk of relying on a single solution.

It also strengthens long-term resilience, preparing organizations for future technological shifts and enabling tailored solutions that meet diverse regulatory requirements and customer needs, such as long-term confidentiality.

Beyond security, cryptographic defence-in-depth fosters expertise, supports innovation and positions organizations to lead in an evolving regulatory and technological landscape.

“

Using diverse technologies is an approach that can already enhance resilience, enable differentiation and prepare organizations for when quantum computers can break cryptography.

”

## Technologies supporting cryptographic defence-in-depth
### Post-quantum cryptography
Multinational organizations operating in these areas should prioritize NIST-approved PQC as the primary quantum-safe technology in their migration.

Organizations with a longer-term outlook may also explore cryptographic defence-in-depth architectures that pair PQC with other quantum-safe techniques for certain use cases.

## Seizing opportunities in the quantum-safe migration
To thrive amid uncertainty, organizations should proactively harness emerging technologies, make informed choices and manage cryptography with long-term resilience and risk management in mind.
